page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an entry-level virtual server configuration powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Managed under KVM virtualization, the instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with multi-threading on a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, backed by 40 MB of L3 cache. The instance features no bundled local disk storage and maintains a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations place the processing and memory throughput metrics in lower percentiles due to the shared core model and legacy CPU generation. Single-core stress-ng tests achieved a score of 945.88, while multi-core performance reached 1857.99. Uncached memory read bandwidth recorded 14.95 GB/sec, with write speeds measuring 11.46 GB/sec. The PassMark CPU test yielded 2538.35, and database operations achieved 558.24. In application-level benchmarks, the instance processed 2.53 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered a static web serving throughput of 2.31 GB/sec.

The ecs.e4.large instance offers qualitative cost efficiency by providing substantial memory capacity on a shared 2-vCPU allocation. The primary hardware tradeoff lies between high RAM density and limited CPU compute performance, as shared core threads can experience latency under sustained execution. The instance is suited for lightweight, memory-bound utility tasks, non-critical Redis caching layers, basic static web serving, and low-traffic internal microservices where dedicated processor capacity is not required.
